classification: C. CONDITIONAL-PRODUCTION CALIBRATION DOES NOT RESOLVE THE PROBLEM
classification_basis: Both preregistered threshold-free location calibrations worsen pooled full-cell CRPS versus frozen D1 and improve only 4 of 9 origins.
Both candidates worsen integrated magnitude-conditioned calibration error and make the supported p75+/p90+/p95+ active-retention compression more negative.
Both candidates improve raw-point MAE by about 2 points and preserve low/mid-source CRPS, showing the fit is numerically coherent but optimizes the wrong tradeoff for Forecast authority.
The fitted common multiplier is below 1 across the magnitude range in every origin; its modest upward curvature at high source magnitude is insufficient to offset the global downshift.
Realized-state diagnostics show opposite-sign conditional-production errors across positive future states at high magnitude, so one common multiplicative location factor is too blunt.
Frozen D1 state probabilities are unchanged and exact control parity passes across all nine Y3 origins.
recommended_next_boundary: Before any new candidate, preregister a bounded identifiability/feasibility test for state-specific threshold-free continuous-magnitude conditional-production calibration (with hierarchical/shared regularization across D1 positive states). The evidence suggests elite/premium and starter/usable conditional means require different corrections; do not reintroduce percentile states or a common global multiplier.
